note.text:
The kinetic theory says:
• All matter is made of tiny particles.
• The particles are always moving. In a solid they vibrate in fixed places; in a liquid they slide past each other; in a gas they move fast in all directions.
• When a substance is heated, its particles gain energy and move faster.
This explains changes of state: when a solid is heated, its particles vibrate so much that they break free (melting); heated more, they escape from the liquid (boiling).
Diffusion: particles spread out from where there are many to where there are few. The smell of ndolé cooking fills the house; a purple crystal colours still water. Diffusion is fastest in gases and faster when warm.

worked_example.problem: Why does the smell of fried plantains reach the next room, even with no wind?
steps: The smell is made of tiny gas particles from the food.
Gas particles move fast in all directions and spread out into the air (diffusion).
They spread from the kitchen, where there are many, to the room, where there are few.
worked_example.answer: The smell particles diffuse through the air.

cards.idea: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.
example: Even in a stone, the particles vibrate in their places.

cards.idea: Heating gives the particles more energy: they move faster. That is why solids melt and liquids boil.
example: Ice melts because its particles vibrate so much that they break free.

cards.idea: Diffusion: particles spread out from where there are many to where there are few. It is fastest in gases and when warm.
example: A drop of ink slowly colours a whole glass of still water.

pick.why: In a solid the particles vibrate in fixed places.
In a liquid the particles slide past each other.
In a gas the particles move fast in all directions.

questions.prompt: In which state do the particles {x.t}?

misconceptions.explain: Think about how freely the particles can move.

questions.prompt: What happens to the particles of a substance when it is heated?

right.text: They gain energy and move faster.

wrong.explain: The particles do not grow; they move faster.
Cooling slows them down; heating speeds them up.
Heating alone does not make new particles in a change of state.

questions.prompt: In which case does diffusion happen fastest?

right.text: a smell spreading through warm air

wrong.text: a smell spreading through cold air
wrong.explain: Diffusion is faster when it is warm: the particles move faster.
Diffusion is much faster in gases than in liquids.

wrong.text: a solid spreading into another solid
wrong.explain: In solids the particles only vibrate: diffusion is extremely slow.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Particles in a gas move fast in all directions.
Diffusion is faster in gases than in liquids.
All matter is made of tiny particles.

wrong.text: Particles in a solid do not move at all.
When ice melts, its particles get bigger.
wrong.explain: The particles move more; they do not get bigger.
